overview.body: BookEx 0 is your setup check, and it has exactly one job: prove that everything works before the real assignments begin. Two very short programs. The first confirms your Python, VS Code, and CodeGrade pipeline is connected end to end. The second confirms you have your textbook and can work from it, because every BookEx after this one is typed straight from the book. Finish both by Sunday and Week 2 will hold no surprises.
objectives: Confirm Python and VS Code are installed and working
Submit a program to CodeGrade and see it pass
Type a short program from the textbook and match its output exactly
overview.keyConceptsText: BookEx 0 previews two ideas from Chapter 2: displaying output with print() and storing a value in a variable. Chapter 2 proper begins next week in BookEx CH02.
overview.textbookReference: Starting Out with Python, 6th Edition by Tony Gaddis — Chapter 2: Input, Processing, and Output (Program 2-4)
programRequirements: Each program is saved as its own individual .py file
Each file uses the exact filename listed in the instructions
Each program runs without syntax errors
Output matches exactly — CodeGrade compares character by character
overview.filenameNote: This chapter uses 10 individual files. Submit all 10 files together in your final CodeGrade submission.

firstTimeCodeGrade.title: First Time Submitting to CodeGrade?
firstTimeCodeGrade.body: This is your first CodeGrade assignment. When you click Submit, you will be prompted to create your CodeGrade account and enter payment. This is a one-time setup — all future submissions go straight through. Have one of these ready: a credit card to pay CodeGrade directly, or an activation code from the campus bookstore.

checkpoints.programRef: Code provided — no textbook needed for this one

Run it and confirm the output reads: Hello, World!
Capital H, capital W, comma, space, exclamation point. CodeGrade compares character by character.

content.title: Copy the Spec, Don't Retype It
content.body: When the instructions show you the exact code or text a program should use, copy and paste it. Zero typos, zero case mistakes. Professionals do this constantly. Save your typing energy for the parts that require thinking.

A four-line program from your textbook that creates a variable, then displays a message and the variable's value. This is your first taste of the pattern every BookEx uses: open the book, type the program exactly as shown, run it, and match the output. It is also a deliberate book check — if you do not have your textbook yet, you will find out now, while there is still time to fix it before Week 2.

items: Create a new file named variable_demo.py.
Type the program exactly as shown in the book.
Run the file and confirm the two output lines match the book.
Fix any typos until it runs cleanly.

content.title: No Book Yet?
content.body: This checkpoint requires the textbook — the code is intentionally not printed here. If your book has not arrived, see the Course Materials section of the syllabus for the eTextbook and Kindle options, both available immediately. Do not wait: every BookEx from here forward is typed from the book.

beforeYouSubmit: hello.py runs and prints exactly: Hello, World!
variable_demo.py runs and both output lines match the book
Both files use the exact filenames listed above
Both files are submitted to CodeGrade and passing

ifYouGetStuck: Re-read the checkpoint and compare your code to the book line by line — a typo is almost always the culprit
Run the program after each checkpoint rather than writing all 10 at once
Submit to CodeGrade early — it shows exactly which files pass and which need work
Post in the course Discord if you are stuck after two attempts (describe the error, do not post your code)
Come to Tuesday office hours if you are still stuck
